# Operator runbook — Packet Review OS

For the person who runs this after the builder leaves.

## Daily use (Maya / hiring coordinator)

1. Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>.
2. Choose the role scorecard (v1 ships `fullstack_engineer`).
3. Paste the packet. Optionally add recruiter notes, upload a resume PDF, or give
   a public job URL.
4. Read the **next action**, the **confidence**, and the **verbatim quotes**.
   The quote is the point: if it does not support the score, send the review back.
5. If you approve, copy the draft into your email client. **This app cannot send
   mail** — there is no mail library in it.
6. Click **Approve this next action** or **Reject / send back**, and leave a note.
7. Use **History** when someone asks "why did we advance X?"

If the banner says the packet is too short, ask the sourcer for a full resume.
Do not proceed on vibes — the system deliberately refuses to score a stub.

## Starting and stopping

```bat
python -m packet_review_os check     :: validate configuration first
python -m packet_review_os serve
```

Stop with Ctrl+C. Data stays in `data/packet_review.db`.

Run `check` after any YAML edit. It prints the exact file and field to fix, and
`serve` refuses to start on a broken scorecard rather than failing on Maya's
first packet.

## Configuration (no code)

| What | Where | Restart needed |
|---|---|---|
| API key, model, port, upload cap, access token | `.env` (copy from `.env.example`) | yes |
| Action thresholds, packet length limits, confidence bands | `config/app.yaml` | yes |
| Role scorecard: criteria, weights, must-haves, knockouts, risk flags | `config/roles/fullstack_engineer.yaml` | yes |

## The two engine modes

- **No `OPENAI_API_KEY` (default).** Grounded extractive engine. Fast, local,
  $0, and every score carries a quote. This is the mode all published evaluation
  numbers come from.
- **With a key.** The model proposes scores and quotes; the action policy still
  runs in code. A quote that is not a verbatim substring of the packet is
  dropped, and an unquoted score above 1 is capped. If the model is down or slow,
  the system falls back to extractive and says so in the banner.

The mode is shown on the form and recorded per review as `engine_mode`.

## Failures you should expect

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "Packet is too short" | Empty paste, or an image-only PDF | Paste the text. Do not force an advance |
| "Could not read PDF" | Scan, encryption, or corruption | Export as text, or paste |
| "is larger than 8 MB" | Oversized upload | Paste the relevant pages |
| "Refusing to fetch … private/internal address" | Job URL points inside your network | Paste the job description text instead |
| "Job URL returned HTTP 404" | Expired posting | Paste the text |
| "LLM unavailable, used the grounded extractive fallback" | No key, quota, outage, or bad JSON | Nothing. The review is complete and grounded |
| "Dropped hallucinated quote on …" | The model invented evidence | Working as intended. Read the remaining quotes |
| Referral went to escalate, not reject | Policy | Correct — founder referrals need a human |
| Strong skills but rejected on conduct | Conduct knockout | Correct. Do not override in the tool; talk to HR |
| 401 page | `API_TOKEN` is set | Open the link that includes `?token=…` |
| Server refuses to start, names a YAML field | Scorecard edit has a mistake | Fix the named field, run `check` |

## Access and exposure

The app binds to `127.0.0.1` by default and needs no password there — only
someone at the keyboard can reach it.

**Before putting it on a network**, set `API_TOKEN` in `.env`:

```bat
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"
```

Then every route except `/health` requires that token. Open the app once as
`http://host:8000/?token=<value>` and it is remembered in a cookie for a day.
`serve` and `check` both warn loudly if you bind publicly without one, because
stored candidate reviews would otherwise be readable by anyone who can reach the
port.

Not built, and needed before real multi-user use: per-user accounts, HTTPS,
audit of who approved what (the store records the decision, not the identity).

## Privacy

- Emails, phone numbers and profile URLs are removed from every stored review —
  including evidence quotes, the draft body and the log lines.
- **Candidate names are kept on purpose.** They are the subject of the review;
  removing them would make the audit log useless.
- Packet text never leaves the machine unless you set an API key. With a key, the
  packet (up to 14,000 characters) is sent to that endpoint. Check your DPA before
  putting real candidate data through a third-party model.
- Never commit `.env` or `data/*.db`. Both are gitignored.
- To delete a candidate's data: `sqlite3 data/packet_review.db "DELETE FROM reviews WHERE run_id='…';"`
  There is no UI for this yet.

## Health and monitoring

```bat
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

Returns `ok`, the version, whether a model is configured, and a count of
configuration problems. It deliberately reveals nothing about candidates, so it
is safe to poll from outside.

## Changing or adding a role

1. Copy `config/roles/fullstack_engineer.yaml` to `config/roles/<new_id>.yaml`.
2. Set `role_id: <new_id>` so it matches the filename. (A mismatch is a
   validation error — copying and forgetting to edit is the common slip.)
3. Edit criteria, weights, must-haves, knockouts and indicators.
4. `python -m packet_review_os check`, then restart.

Keep must-haves explicit and few. **Never encode illegal or discriminatory
criteria** — age, family status, national origin, or any protected class.
Work authorisation is a `request_missing_info`, never an auto-reject.

Adding a role does not require Python changes, but it does invalidate the
evaluation: the gold set covers `fullstack_engineer` only. Write cases for a new
role before trusting its output.

## When to page a human (always)

- Any `escalate_to_hiring_manager` result
- Any conduct knockout
- Any disagreement between a quote and your own reading of the packet
- Any internal employee or executive candidate
- Confidence labelled **low**

## Verifying the system still works

```bat
python -m packet_review_os eval    :: 12 gold cases + 6 model-path + 7 fixtures
pytest -q                          :: 216 unit and integration tests
```

`eval` exits non-zero if any case lands outside its allowed action set or any
invariant breaks. Run it after every YAML change — a threshold edit that looks
harmless can move several cases.

## Rollback

If quality drops after a config edit, revert the file (`git checkout --
config/roles/fullstack_engineer.yaml`), run `check`, and restart. The database
schema is versioned and migrates forward automatically; no rollback is needed
for v1 → v1.1.
